title: Backfill historical time-to-ready metrics from logs for baseline + before/after comparison
creator: Jamal Pierce
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
content:
## Context
We need a reliable baseline for Dedicated pool bring-up lead times prior to the new provision-to-ready automation. The live metrics we’re adding (ENG-2748) will cover new runs, but Sales/CS + SRE need:

1) historical p50/p95 time-to-ready over the last ~10 pool bring-ups
2) stage-level breakdown (even if approximate) to validate where time is currently going
3) a before/after comparison once the pilot automation runs (week 4) complete

This ticket is specifically the *backfill* from existing logs/events into an analysis dataset + summary.

## Goals / deliverables
- Build a backfill job that extracts historical provisioning timelines from log archives and produces:
  - per-run time-to-ready (Requested -> Ready)
  - per-stage durations where possible (Provisioning / Imaging / Bootstrapping / Validating)
  - flags for incomplete/ambiguous runs
- Produce a baseline report (p50/p95 + top delay causes) for the last 10 bring-ups.
- Produce a before/after snapshot comparing baseline vs pilot automation runs.

## Non-goals
- Perfect reconstruction of all stage transitions (historical logs are inconsistent). We will provide best-effort stage inference and clearly tag “estimated” vs “exact”.
- Replacing the canonical metrics pipeline (ENG-2748/PR-48232/PR-48239). This is an offline backfill + analysis.

## Data sources
- Control plane service logs: pool registration + ready-marking messages.
- Fleet ops / provisioner logs: terraform apply start/finish, imaging start/finish, bootstrap hooks.
- Perf-canary logs (for pilot runs only) for Validating->Ready gating confirmation.

We are pulling from the central log archive (S3) via Athena queries for the time range 2023-11-01 .. 2024-02-20.

## Approach
### 1) Define canonical stage mapping (historical)
Because pre-automation logs don’t have a consistent state machine, we map events into the current stage model:
- Requested: earliest “pool expansion requested” event (or Jira/Slack reference when missing)
- Provisioning: terraform apply start -> terraform apply success
- Imaging: image bake / cloud-init completion markers; fallback to "node joined cluster" time if missing
- Bootstrapping: helm bootstrap start -> helm bootstrap success (or first successful runtime pod Ready)
- Validating: first readiness checks start -> perf-canary pass (pilot runs) OR first successful runtime smoke test (historical)
- Ready: control plane marks pool Ready (or first time routing advertises pool, if control plane message missing)

Each stage duration is tagged as:
- exact: start and end from explicit log events
- inferred: one boundary inferred from nearby event(s)
- missing: cannot compute

### 2) Correlation strategy
Historical logs often lack a stable correlation_id. We join on:
- pool_id (preferred)
- region + cluster_name + approximate timestamp window (fallback)
- terraform workspace name (fallback)

We store a join_confidence score (high/medium/low) so we can exclude low-confidence runs from headline stats.

### 3) Output dataset + summary
- Write results to `analytics.dedicated_time_to_ready_backfill` (one row per pool bring-up / expansion run).
- Publish a short report + linkable queries for Jamal/SRE/Product.
- Generate before/after using:
  - baseline cohort: 10 most recent runs before feature-flag pilot
  - pilot cohort: runs executed through new pipeline (post-flag)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Dataset contains >= 10 historical runs with overall time-to-ready and at least 3 stage durations populated for >= 70% of runs.
- [x] Summary includes p50/p95 overall time-to-ready and p50/p95 per stage (for stages with sufficient data).
- [x] Before/after comparison for pilot runs is generated with the same stage definitions.
- [x] Artifacts linked in this ticket (Drive doc + saved queries / dashboard link).

## Artifacts
- Drive (baseline analysis): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-inference/shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/time-to-ready-baseline-analysis
- Drive (stage timing table): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-inference/shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/time-to-ready-stage-timings
- Confluence overview (stage definitions): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/INFRA/Provision-to-ready+automation+overview

## Results (baseline)
Cohort: 10 Dedicated pool bring-ups/expansions (2023-11 .. 2024-02), excluding 2 low-confidence correlations.

Headline:
- Overall time-to-ready:
  - p50: 9h 40m
  - p95: 26h 15m
- Biggest contributors (median stage duration):
  - Imaging: 3h 05m (high variance; regional artifact mirror issues show up here)
  - Bootstrapping: 2h 20m (helm values drift / retries)
  - Provisioning (Terraform): 1h 50m (quota/IAM + manual retries)

Top delay causes (tagged from error patterns + operator notes):
- Imaging timeouts / slow pulls (notably in one region)
- Terraform retries due to quota or IAM drift
- Bootstrap failures due to misconfigured helm values + manual intervention

## Results (pilot before/after)
Pilot cohort: 2 internal pools + 1 customer expansion executed under the provisioning feature flag.

- Overall time-to-ready:
  - baseline p50 (above): 9h 40m
  - pilot p50: 4h 15m
- Notes:
  - Provisioning improved mostly due to fewer manual retries + clearer preflight failures.
  - Imaging is still the largest tail risk (p95 not meaningful at n=3; needs more runs).

## Follow-ups / gaps
- Add explicit "requested" event emission to avoid relying on Slack/Jira timestamps for future analysis.
- After 10+ pilot/prod runs, re-run before/after with a statistically meaningful cohort.
- Consider making join_confidence visible on the dashboard so SRE can filter quickly.

---

## Updates
### 2024-02-21 (Logan)
Pulled the list of last 12 Dedicated bring-ups from infra notes + pool registry. Starting with log archive queries keyed by pool_id. Biggest risk: missing correlation between terraform logs and control plane logs.

### 2024-02-23 (Logan)
Drafted event->stage mapping. Found 3 runs with no explicit Ready mark in control plane logs; can use routing advertisement timestamp as fallback but will label as inferred.

### 2024-02-27 (Logan)
First pass dataset generated (12 runs). join_confidence: 8 high / 2 medium / 2 low. Excluding low from headline stats. Shared preliminary numbers with Jamal + Aisha in #eng-sre.

### 2024-03-01 (Aisha review)
Requested that we break out Imaging vs Bootstrapping clearly (previous baseline lumped them together). Also asked for p95 per stage where possible.

### 2024-03-05 (Logan)
Updated queries to separate stages + added join_confidence + stage_quality fields (exact/inferred/missing). Baseline doc updated.

### 2024-03-12 (Logan)
Added pilot runs (feature flag) to comparison cohort. Noted that perf-canary completion is the cleanest Validating->Ready boundary; historical runs use smoke test timestamps.

### 2024-03-18 (Jamal)
Baseline + before/after summary is in the Drive doc and numbers match what we’ve been using in planning. Marking done; follow-up work goes into dashboard improvements and additional cohorts once we have more runs.
